sentences.text: This dinosaur is estimated to have reached a length of 25 meters.
Lü Junchang, Yi Laiping, Zhong Hui, and Wei Xuefang first named Gannansaurus in 2013.
Most of the original specimen was destroyed during construction, but one dorsal vertebra was reconstructed from fragments.
The two preserved vertebrae are stored at the Ganzhou Museum of Natural History with the catalog number GMNH F10001.
Gannansaurus is more closely related to Euhelopus than to other titanosauriforms based on shared characters.
A 2023 phylogenetic analysis recovered Gannansaurus as a basal titanosauriform.
The animal belongs to the unranked family Somphospondyli.
Gannansaurus lived during the late Upper Cretaceous, approximately between 72 and 66 million years ago in the Maastrichtian.
The time range for Gannansaurus is the Maastrichtian, from 72.2 to 66 million years ago.
